page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n1 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, categorized as weak, while the multi-core score drops to a poor rating of 1408.88. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.82 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 13.22 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these limitations, with a Passmark CPU score of 1638.85 and a Redis SET performance of 1.35 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-2 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 2.0 GB alongside its low benchmark scores across database and computational tasks. However, its dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution compared to shared-core alternatives. This profile is qualitatively cost-effective for lightweight, compute-focused tasks that do not demand significant memory footprints, such as basic static web serving, simple background scripting, or low-intensity development and testing environments.
